translations.literal: He Fengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: He Fengsheng.

translations.idiomatic: (Fu Guan and Yin Ruweng)〉

translations.literal: Nan Juyi.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Juyi.

translations.literal: (Clan elder Qi Zhong; clan younger brother Juye)〉
translations.idiomatic: (His clan elder Qi Zhong and younger clansman Juye)〉

translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shipu and Lu Weiqi.

translations.idiomatic: (His younger brother Lu Weineng)〉

translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiazhen and Jiao Yuanpu.

sentences.zh: 李夢辰宋師襄麻僖王道純田時震

translations.literal: Li Mengchen; Song Shixiang; Ma Xi; Wang Daochun; Tian Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengchen, Song Shixiang, Ma Xi, Wang Daochun, and Tian Shizhen.

translations.literal: (Zhu Chongde; Chongde's son Zhu Guodong)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zhu Chongde and Chongde's son Zhu Guodong)〉

sentences.zh: 賀逢聖，字克繇，江夏人。

translations.literal: He Fengsheng, courtesy name Keyao, was a native of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He Fengsheng, styled Keyao, came from Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 與熊廷弼少同里闬，而不相能。

translations.literal: He and Xiong Tingbi had been neighbors in youth, yet they could not get along.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xiong Tingbi grew up in the same neighborhood but never got along.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，同受知於督學熊尚文。

translations.literal: As students they were both noticed by the education intendant Xiong Shangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Both were licentiates whom the education intendant Xiong Shangwen favored.

sentences.zh: 尚文並奇二生，曰：「熊生，幹將、莫邪也；

translations.literal: Shangwen admired both students and said: "Student Xiong is Ganjiang and Moye;
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen praised them both, saying, "Xiong is Ganjiang and Moye—

sentences.zh: 賀生，夏瑚、商璉也。」

translations.literal: student He is Xia's coral and Shang's jade disks.
translations.idiomatic: He is the coral of Xia and the ritual disks of Shang.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 家貧，就應城教諭。

translations.literal: His family was poor, and he took a post as instructor in Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Poor at home, he accepted a post as county instructor in Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年，殿試第二人，授翰林編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he placed second in the palace examination and was made Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 44 he ranked second in the palace examination and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 天啟間，為洗馬。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he served as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he served as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 當是時，廷弼已再起經略遼東矣。

translations.literal: At that time Tingbi had already been reappointed to command Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiong Tingbi had already been restored to command in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 廣寧之敗，同鄉官將揭白廷弼之冤，意逢聖且沮之。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Guangning, fellow-townsmen officials were about to expose Tingbi's injustice, expecting Fengsheng would obstruct them.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangning fell, hometown officials meant to clear Tingbi's name, fearing Fengsheng would block them.

sentences.zh: 逢聖作色曰：「此乃國家大事，吾安敢小嫌介介，不以明！」

translations.literal: Fengsheng flushed and said: "This is a matter of state—how dare I let petty grudges keep me from making it clear!"
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng flushed and said, "This is a matter of state—how could I let a private feud keep the truth hidden!"

sentences.zh: 即具草上之。

translations.literal: He at once drafted a memorial and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a memorial at once and sent it up.

sentences.zh: 湖廣建魏忠賢生祠，忠賢聞上梁文出逢聖手，大喜，即日詣逢聖。

translations.literal: Huguang built a living shrine to Wei Zhongxian; Zhongxian heard the beam-raising inscription was Fengsheng's work, was greatly pleased, and called on Fengsheng that same day.
translations.idiomatic: When Huguang raised a shrine to Wei Zhongxian, Zhongxian learned the beam inscription was Fengsheng's and came to see him the same day, delighted.

sentences.zh: 逢聖曰：「誤，借銜陋習耳。」

translations.literal: Fengsheng said: "A mistake—merely an old habit of lending my name."
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng said, "A mistake—just an old habit of lending my name."

sentences.zh: 忠賢咈然去。

translations.literal: Zhongxian left in a huff.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian stalked off in a fury.

sentences.zh: 翌日削逢聖籍。

translations.literal: The next day Fengsheng was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fengsheng was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，復官，連進秩。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor came to the throne, Fengsheng was restored and promoted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhen acceded, Fengsheng was restored and promoted again and again.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，以禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，入閣輔政，加太子太保，改文淵閣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year he was made Minister of Rites and concurrent Grand Secretary of the Eastern Lodge, entered the Grand Council to assist in government, was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and transferred to the Wenyuan Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year nine he became Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Lodge, entered the Grand Council, was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and moved to the Wenyuan Lodge.

sentences.zh: 十一年致政。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 十四年再入閣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he re-entered the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he returned to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 明年再致政。

translations.literal: The following year he retired again.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he retired once more.

sentences.zh: 逢聖為人廉靜，束修砥行。

translations.literal: Fengsheng was by nature frugal and quiet, strict in conduct and upright in action.
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng was frugal and reserved, austere and upright in conduct.

sentences.zh: 帝頗事操切，逢聖終無所匡言。

translations.literal: The emperor was rather severe in policy, yet Fengsheng in the end offered no corrective remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled harshly, yet Fengsheng never truly corrected him.

sentences.zh: 其再與周延儒同召，帝待之不如延儒。

translations.literal: When he was summoned again together with Zhou Yanru, the emperor treated him less favorably than Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Called back with Zhou Yanru, he was treated less warmly than Yanru.

sentences.zh: 及予告，宴餞便殿，賜金，賜坐蟒。

translations.literal: When he asked leave, the emperor feasted him in the side hall, bestowed gold, and granted python robes for seated wear.
translations.idiomatic: On his retirement the emperor feasted him in the side hall, gave him gold, and granted python robes for seated wear.

sentences.zh: 感激大哭，伏地不能起，帝亦汍瀾動容焉。

translations.literal: Moved to tears of gratitude, he prostrated himself and could not rise; the emperor too was stirred to tears.
translations.idiomatic: He wept in gratitude and could not rise from the ground; the emperor's face also brimmed with tears.

sentences.zh: 是時，湖廣賊大擾。

translations.literal: At that time bandits in Huguang were greatly disturbing the region.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were then ravaging Huguang.

sentences.zh: 明年春，張獻忠連陷蘄、黃，逼江夏。

translations.literal: The next spring Zhang Xianzhong seized Qizhou and Huangzhou in succession and pressed upon Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring Zhang Xianzhong took Qizhou and Huangzhou in turn and closed on Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 有大冶人尹如翁，逢聖門生，走三百里，持一僧帽、一袈裟來貽逢聖。

translations.literal: A man of Daye named Yin Ruweng, Fengsheng's student, traveled three hundred li and brought a monk's cap and a kasaya robe as gifts to Fengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ruweng of Daye, Fengsheng's pupil, walked three hundred li to bring him a monk's cap and kasaya.

sentences.zh: 逢聖反其衣曰：「子第去，毋憂我。」

translations.literal: Fengsheng returned the garments and said: "You had best leave—do not worry for me."
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng handed the robes back and said, "Go now—do not worry about me."

sentences.zh: 如翁去。

translations.literal: Ruweng departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruweng left.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌晦，賊陷武昌，執逢聖，叱曰：「我朝廷大臣，若曹敢無禮！」

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the last day renxu, the bandits took Wuchang, seized Fengsheng, and he shouted: "I am a minister of the court—how dare you people be rude!"
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the fifth month, renxu, the rebels took Wuchang and seized Fengsheng, who cried, "I am a minister of the court—how dare you treat me so!"

sentences.zh: 賊麾使去，遂投墩子湖死也。

translations.literal: The bandits waved him away, and he thereupon cast himself into Dunzi Lake and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels motioned him away; he threw himself into Dunzi Lake and died.

sentences.zh: 賊來自夏，去以秋雲。

translations.literal: The bandits came in summer and departed like autumn clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came in summer and drifted away like autumn clouds.

sentences.zh: 大吏望衍而祭，有神夢於湖之人，「我守賀相殊苦，汝受而視之，有黑子在其左手，其征是。」

translations.literal: The great officials gazed toward the shallows and made offerings; a spirit dreamed to a man by the lake: "I have guarded Chancellor He with great hardship—take him and look: there is a black mole on his left hand; that is the sign."
translations.idiomatic: High officials prayed toward the shallows; a spirit appeared in a lakeside dream: "I have guarded Chancellor He with great pain—take him up and look: a black mole on his left hand will prove it."

sentences.zh: 覺而異之，俟於湖，赫然而屍出，驗之果是，蓋沈之百有七十日，面如生。

translations.literal: On waking they marveled, waited by the lake, and the corpse emerged with sudden brightness; on examination it was indeed he—he had been submerged one hundred and seventy days, yet his face was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Awake, they wondered, waited at the lake, and his body rose suddenly from the water; it was indeed he, submerged one hundred and seventy days yet lifelike in the face.

sentences.zh: 以冬十一月壬子殮，大吏揮淚而葬之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on day renzi, he was encoffined; the great officials wept as they buried him.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the eleventh winter month he was encoffined, and the great officials buried him through tears.

sentences.zh: 初，城之陷也，逢聖載家人以其句鹿出墩子，鑿其氐當，皆溺。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the city fell, Fengsheng loaded his family into his square-stern boat to leave by Dunzi, bored holes in its bottom, and all drowned.
translations.idiomatic: When the city first fell, Fengsheng put his family in his square-stern boat at Dunzi, bored holes in the hull, and all drowned.

sentences.zh: 賀氏死者，妻危氏，子覲明，子婦曾氏、陳氏，孫三人，次子光明自他所來，凡二十余人。

translations.literal: Among the dead of the He clan were his wife Lady Wei, his son Jingming, daughters-in-law the Ladies Zeng and Chen, three grandsons, and his second son Guangming who had come from elsewhere—in all more than twenty persons.
translations.idiomatic: The He dead included his wife Lady Wei, his son Jingming, daughters-in-law Ladies Zeng and Chen, three grandsons, and his second son Guangming, who had come from elsewhere—more than twenty in all.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈少傅，謚文忠，祭葬蔭子如制。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Junior Tutor, given the posthumous title Wenzong, and granted sacrificial burial and hereditary privilege for his sons according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Junior Tutor, titled Wenzong, and given state burial and hereditary honors for his sons as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 如翁去，歸大冶。

translations.literal: Ruweng departed and returned to Daye.
translations.idiomatic: Ruweng went home to Daye.

sentences.zh: 大冶城破，其慷慨而死者，如翁也。

translations.literal: When Daye's walls fell, among those who died in generous resolve was Ruweng.
translations.idiomatic: When Daye fell, Ruweng was among those who died defiantly.

sentences.zh: 其後有傅冠。

translations.literal: After him there was Fu Guan.
translations.idiomatic: After him came Fu Guan.

sentences.zh: 冠，字元甫，進賢人。

translations.literal: Guan, courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Guan, styled Yuanfu, came from Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 祖炯，南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiong was Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiong had been Nanjing Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，冠舉進士第二，授翰林編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi Guan placed second among jinshi and was made Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he ranked second among jinshi and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年秋，由禮部右侍郎拜尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year of Chongzhen he was promoted from Vice Minister of Rites to Minister and concurrent Grand Secretary of the Eastern Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Chongzhen 10 he rose from Vice Minister of Rites to Minister and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Lodge.

sentences.zh: 性簡易，有章奏發自御前，冠以為揭帖，援筆判其上。

translations.literal: His nature was plain and easygoing; when a memorial issued from the imperial presence, Guan took it for a routine note and wrote a judgment upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and easygoing by nature, he mistook an imperial memorial for a routine note and wrote a verdict on it.

sentences.zh: 既知誤，惶恐引罪，帝即放歸。

translations.literal: Once he knew his error he confessed in fear, and the emperor at once sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: When he realized the mistake he confessed in terror, and the emperor sent him home at once.

sentences.zh: 唐王時，命以原官督師江西。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Tang he was ordered to command troops in Jiangxi with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Tang he was ordered to command in Jiangxi at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒，或劾之，乃致仕。

translations.literal: He was fond of wine; some impeached him, and he then retired.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of wine, he was impeached and retired.

sentences.zh: 大清下江西，冠走匿門人泰寧汪亨龍家。

translations.literal: When the Great Qing took Jiangxi, Guan fled and hid in the home of his student Wang Henglong of Taining.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing took Jiangxi, Guan fled and hid with his pupil Wang Henglong of Taining.

sentences.zh: 亨龍執而獻之有司，殺之汀州，血漬地，久而猶鮮。

translations.literal: Henglong seized him and handed him to the authorities; he was executed at Tingzhou, and the blood that stained the ground long remained bright.
translations.idiomatic: Henglong seized him and handed him over; he was killed at Tingzhou, and his blood on the ground stayed bright for a long time.

sentences.zh: 南居益，字思受，渭南人，尚書企仲族子、師仲從子也。

translations.literal: Nan Juyi, courtesy name Sishou, was a native of Weinan, a clansman of the Minister Qi Zhong and nephew of Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Juyi, styled Sishou, came from Weinan; he was a clansman of Minister Qi Zhong and nephew of Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖從吉與曾伯祖大吉皆進士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Congji and great-great-uncle Daji were both jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Congji and great-great-uncle Daji had both been jinshi.

sentences.zh: 兩人子姓，科第相繼。

translations.literal: The sons of both men passed the examinations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Their sons and grandsons won degrees in succession.

sentences.zh: 企仲，大吉孫，萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: Qi Zhong, grandson of Daji, became jinshi in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zhong, Daji's grandson, took the jinshi in Wanli 8.

sentences.zh: 以祖母年高，請終養。

translations.literal: Because his grandmother was advanced in years, he requested leave to care for her until death.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother being old, he asked leave to nurse her to the end.

sentences.zh: 祖母既歿，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: After his grandmother died he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After she died he was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 客寓貲其家，夫婦並歿，企仲呼其子還之。

translations.literal: A lodger had entrusted goods to his household; husband and wife both died, and Qi Zhong summoned the lodger's son to return them.
translations.idiomatic: A lodger had left goods with his household; when both husband and wife died, Qi Zhong called the lodger's son to return them.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書孫丕揚以為賢，調為己屬。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Sun Piyang considered him worthy and transferred him to his own staff.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Piyang, Minister of Personnel, thought him worthy and took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 歷文選郎，擢太僕少卿，進太僕卿。

translations.literal: He served as an officer in the Bureau of Appointments, was promoted Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, and advanced to Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Bureau of Appointments to Vice Minister and then Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 三十年，帝以疾詔免礦稅，釋系囚，錄建言貶斥諸臣。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, because of illness the emperor issued an edict abolishing mining taxes, releasing prisoners, and restoring officials demoted for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty the emperor, ill, abolished mining taxes, freed prisoners, and restored officials banished for speaking out.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，命礦稅如故，余所司議行。

translations.literal: Soon he regretted it and ordered mining taxes as before; the rest was left to the relevant offices to carry out as they saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted it, restored the mining taxes, and let the rest be handled as each office saw fit.

sentences.zh: 吏、刑二部尚書李戴、蕭大亨遲數日未奏，企仲請亟罷二人，而敕二部亟如詔奉行。

translations.literal: The Ministers of Personnel and Justice, Li Dai and Xiao Daheng, delayed several days without memorializing; Qi Zhong asked that both be dismissed at once and that the two ministries be ordered to carry out the edict immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dai and Xiao Daheng of Personnel and Justice delayed for days; Qi Zhong urged their immediate dismissal and ordered both ministries to obey the edict at once.

sentences.zh: 帝大恚，傳諭亟停二事，落企仲一官。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, sent word to stop both matters at once, and demoted Qi Zhong one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, ordered both matters stopped at once, and demoted Qi Zhong one rank.

sentences.zh: 給事中蕭近高，御史李培、余懋衡亦請信明詔，帝益怒，並奪其俸，且命益重前貶謫官鄒元標等罰，欲以鉗言者。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Xiao Jingao and the censors Li Pei and Yu Maoheng also asked that the clear edict be trusted; the emperor grew still angrier, stripped all of their salaries, and ordered heavier penalties on the previously demoted official Zou Yuanbiao and others, intending to silence speakers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jingao and censors Li Pei and Yu Maoheng also urged trust in the edict; the emperor grew angrier still, stripped their salaries, and ordered heavier punishments on Zou Yuanbiao and others to silence critics.

sentences.zh: 諸閣臣力爭，乃止。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretaries argued strenuously, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretaries argued hard, and he relented.

sentences.zh: 而給事中張鳳翔迎帝意，劾企仲他事，遂削籍。

translations.literal: But the supervising secretary Zhang Fengxiang, courting the emperor's mood, impeached Qi Zhong on other matters, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fengxiang, courting the emperor's mood, impeached Qi Zhong on other grounds and had him struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，起太常卿，累遷南京吏部尚書，以老致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was recalled as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, was promoted in succession to Nanjing Minister of Personnel, and retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he was recalled as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, rose to Nanjing Minister of Personnel, and retired in old age.

sentences.zh: 師仲父軒，吏部郎中，嘗著《通鑒綱目前編》。

translations.literal: Shizhong's father Xuan was a director in the Ministry of Personnel and once compiled the Preliminary Compilation to the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong's father Xuan, a director in the Ministry of Personnel, had compiled a preliminary draft of the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 師仲至南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shizhong rose to Nanjing Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong rose to Nanjing Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 居益少厲操行，舉萬歷二十九年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Juyi from youth was strict in conduct; he became jinshi in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi was strict in conduct from youth; he took the jinshi in Wanli 29 and became a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 三遷廣平知府，擢山西提學副使，雁門參政，歷按察使、左右布政使，並在山西。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became prefect of Guangping, was raised to Vice Commissioner of Education in Shanxi, then Pacification Commissioner at Yanmen, and served in succession as surveillance commissioner and left and right administration commissioners—all in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted thrice, he became prefect of Guangping, then Shanxi Vice Commissioner of Education, Yanmen Pacification Commissioner, and in turn surveillance commissioner and left and right administration commissioners—all in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，入為太仆卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he entered the capital as Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he entered the capital as Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 明年擢右副都御史，巡撫福建。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 紅毛夷者，海外雜種，紺眼，赤須發，所謂和蘭國也，自昔不通中土，由大泥、咬𠺕吧二國通閩商。

translations.literal: The Red-Haired barbarians were a mixed race beyond the seas, with indigo eyes and red beards and hair—the so-called country of Holland—which from old had not communicated with the Central Land and reached Fujian merchants through the two countries of Da Ni and Malacca.
translations.idiomatic: The Red-Haired foreigners were a mixed overseas people with indigo eyes and red hair—the so-called Holland—never in direct contact with China, reaching Fujian traders through Da Ni and Malacca.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，奸民潘秀引其人據彭湖求市，巡撫徐學聚令轉販之二國。

translations.literal: During Wanli the scoundrel Pan Xiu led them to occupy Penghu and seek trade; Grand Coordinator Xu Xueju ordered them to divert their trade to the two countries.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli the rogue Pan Xiu brought them to Penghu to trade; Grand Coordinator Xu Xueju told them to trade through the two countries instead.

sentences.zh: 二國險遠，商舍而之呂宋。

translations.literal: The two countries were perilous and remote, and the merchants abandoned them for Luzon.
translations.idiomatic: Those routes being dangerous and remote, merchants turned to Luzon.

sentences.zh: 夷人疑呂宋邀商舶，攻之，又寇廣東香山澳，皆敗，不敢歸國，復入彭湖求市，且築城焉。

translations.literal: The barbarians suspected Luzon was intercepting merchant vessels, attacked it, then raided Xiangshan Anchorage in Guangdong—all were defeated, they dared not return home, re-entered Penghu to seek trade, and even built a fort there.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting Luzon of seizing merchant ships, they attacked it, then raided Xiangshan Anchorage in Guangdong; defeated everywhere, they dared not go home, returned to Penghu to trade, and built a fort.

sentences.zh: 巡撫商周祚拒之，不能靖。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Shang Zhouzuo refused them but could not restore peace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Shang Zhouzuo refused them but could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 會居益代周祚，賊方犯漳、泉，招日本、大泥、咬𠺕吧及海寇李旦等為助。

translations.literal: When Juyi replaced Zhouzuo, the bandits were just then attacking Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, recruiting Japan, Da Ni, Malacca, and the sea bandit Li Dan and others as allies.
translations.idiomatic: When Juyi replaced Zhouzuo, the raiders were attacking Zhangzhou and Quanzhou and had enlisted Japan, Da Ni, Malacca, and the pirate Li Dan.

sentences.zh: 居益使人招旦，說攜大泥、咬𠺕吧。

translations.literal: Juyi sent men to recruit Dan and persuaded him to bring Da Ni and Malacca over.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi sent envoys to win Li Dan and persuaded him to bring Da Ni and Malacca with him.

sentences.zh: 賊帥高文律懼，遣使求款，斬之，築城鎮海港，逼賊風櫃。

translations.literal: The bandit leader Gao Wenlü was afraid, sent envoys to sue for peace; Juyi beheaded them, built a fort at Zhenhai Harbor, and pressed the bandits' anchorage at Fenggui.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Gao Wenlü, afraid, sent envoys to sue for peace; Juyi beheaded them, fortified Zhenhai Harbor, and pressed the rebels' anchorage at Fenggui.

sentences.zh: 賊窮蹙，泛舟去，遂擒文律，海患乃息。

translations.literal: The bandits were cornered, put to sea in boats and fled; Wenlü was then captured, and the maritime trouble ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, the raiders took to their boats and fled; Wenlü was captured and the sea raids ended.

sentences.zh: 五年遷工部右侍郎，總督河道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and made Grand Coordinator of the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he became Vice Minister of Works and Grand Coordinator of the waterways.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢銜居益敘功不及己，格其賞。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian resented that Juyi's report of merit did not mention him and blocked his reward.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian, angry that Juyi's merit report omitted him, blocked his reward.

sentences.zh: 給事中黃承昊復論居益倚傍門戶，躐躋通顯，遂削籍去。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Huang Chenghao again argued that Juyi relied on factional patronage and leapt to high office; he was struck from the rolls and left.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chenghao charged that Juyi had climbed through factional patronage; he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 閩人詣闕訟之，不聽。

translations.literal: Fujian people went to the capital to plead on his behalf, but were not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Fujianese went to court to plead for him, but were not heard.

sentences.zh: 乃立祠以祀，勒碑於彭湖及平遠臺。

translations.literal: They then erected a shrine to worship him and carved stelae at Penghu and Pingyuan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: They raised a shrine to him and set up stelae at Penghu and Pingyuan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起戶部右侍郎，總督倉場。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue and made Grand Coordinator of the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Coordinator of the granaries.

sentences.zh: 陜西鎮缺餉至三十余月，居益請以陜賦當輸關門者留三十萬，紓其急，報可。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi garrison had lacked pay for more than thirty months; Juyi asked that three hundred thousand of the Shaanxi tax due at Tongmen be retained to ease the crisis, and approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi troops had gone unpaid for more than thirty months; Juyi secured approval to retain three hundred thousand taels of Shaanxi tax bound for Tongmen.

sentences.zh: 畿輔戒嚴，居益在通州，為城守計甚備。

translations.literal: The capital region was on alert; Juyi was at Tongzhou and made very thorough plans for defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital region on alert, Juyi at Tongzhou made thorough plans for the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 會工部尚書張鳳翔坐軍械不具下吏，四司郎中瘐死者三，遂詔居益代鳳翔。

translations.literal: When Minister of Works Zhang Fengxiang was sent to the magistrates for deficient armaments and three directors of the four bureaus died of illness, Juyi was ordered to replace Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fengxiang was prosecuted for deficient armaments and three bureau directors died, Juyi was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，試炮而炸，兵部尚書梁廷棟劾郎中王守履失職。

translations.literal: Before long a trial firing of cannon exploded; Minister of War Liang Tingdong impeached the director Wang Shoulü for dereliction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a cannon trial exploded; Minister of War Liang Tingdong impeached Director Wang Shoulü.

sentences.zh: 守履懼，詆兵部郎中王建侯誣己。

translations.literal: Shoulü in fear slandered the Ministry of War director Wang Jianhou, claiming he had framed him.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Shoulü claimed Wang Jianhou of the Ministry of War had framed him.

sentences.zh: 廷議不如守履言，遂下獄。

translations.literal: Court discussion did not support Shoulü's claim, and he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejected his claim and sent him to prison.

sentences.zh: 居益疏捄，帝以為徇私，削籍歸。

translations.literal: Juyi memorialized to save him; the emperor thought it favoritism and struck Juyi from the rolls, sending him home.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi memorialized in his defense; the emperor called it favoritism, struck Juyi from the rolls, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 廷杖守履六十，斥為民。

translations.literal: Shoulü was given sixty strokes at court and dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Shoulü received sixty strokes at court and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋敘城守功，復居益冠帶。

translations.literal: Soon, recounting his merit in defending the city, Juyi's cap and belt were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his merit in the city's defense was recognized and his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 十六年，李自成陷渭南，責南氏餉百六十萬。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Li Zicheng took Weinan and demanded one million six hundred thousand in provisions from the Nan clan.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen Li Zicheng took Weinan and demanded 1.6 million in provisions from the Nan family.

sentences.zh: 企仲年八十三矣，遇害。

translations.literal: Qi Zhong was eighty-three and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zhong, aged eighty-three, was killed.

sentences.zh: 誘降居益及企仲子禮部主事居業，皆不從。

translations.literal: They tried to induce Juyi and Qi Zhong's son Juye, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites, to surrender; neither would yield.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to win over Juyi and Qi Zhong's son Juye, a Ministry of Rites clerk; both refused.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，賊遣兵擁之去，加炮烙。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the bandits sent troops to drag them away and applied branding torture.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month rebels dragged them away and tortured them with branding irons.

sentences.zh: 二人終不屈，絕食七日而死。

translations.literal: The two men would not yield to the end; after seven days without food they died.
translations.idiomatic: Neither yielded; after seven days without food they died.

sentences.zh: 周士樸，字丹其，商丘人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shipu, courtesy name Danqi, was a native of Shangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shipu, styled Danqi, came from Shangqiu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He became jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Wanli 41.

sentences.zh: 除曲沃知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Quwo.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Quwo.

sentences.zh: 泰昌元年征授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang he was summoned and made supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang 1 he was summoned as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 中官王添爵選凈身男子，索賄激變。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch Wang Tianjue selected candidates for castration and demanded bribes, provoking a riot.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Tianjue, selecting candidates for castration, demanded bribes and provoked a riot.

sentences.zh: 守陵劉尚忠鼓陵軍挾賞。

translations.literal: Liu Shangzhong, guardian of the imperial tombs, incited the tomb guards to extort rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb guardian Liu Shangzhong incited the tomb guards to extort rewards.

sentences.zh: 劉朝等假賫送軍器名，出行山海外，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: Liu Chao and others, under the pretense of delivering military stores, traveled beyond the mountains and seas with menacing force.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao and others traveled beyond the passes ostensibly delivering arms, their retinue menacing.

sentences.zh: 織造李實訐周起元。

translations.literal: The weaving intendant Li Shi denounced Zhou Qiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Weaving intendant Li Shi denounced Zhou Qiyuan.

sentences.zh: 群珰索冬衣，辱尚書鐘羽正。

translations.literal: A crowd of eunuchs demanded winter garments and insulted Minister Zhong Yuzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs demanded winter garments and insulted Minister Zhong Yuzheng.

sentences.zh: 士樸皆疏爭。

translations.literal: Shipu memorialized in protest on every count.
translations.idiomatic: Shipu protested each abuse in memorials.

sentences.zh: 士樸性剛果，不能委蛇隨俗，尤好與中官相搘柱，深為魏忠賢所惡。

translations.literal: Shipu was by nature firm and resolute, unable to bend with the times, and especially fond of opposing palace eunuchs; Wei Zhongxian hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Firm and unable to bend with the times, he especially loved to block palace eunuchs, and Wei Zhongxian hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 會當擢京卿，忠賢持不下，士樸遂謝病歸。

translations.literal: When he was due for promotion to a capital minister, Zhongxian held it back; Shipu then asked leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Due for promotion to a capital post, he was blocked by Zhongxian and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十五年，廷臣交薦，不召。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year court officials recommended him in succession, but he was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen the court repeatedly recommended him, but he was not recalled.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，李自成陷商丘，與妻曹、妾張、子舉人業熙、子婦沈同日縊死。

translations.literal: That eighth month Li Zicheng took Shangqiu; he, his wife Lady Cao, concubine Lady Zhang, his son the licentiate Yexi, and daughter-in-law Lady Shen hanged themselves on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: That August Li Zicheng took Shangqiu; Shipu, his wife Lady Cao, concubine Lady Zhang, his licentiate son Yexi, and daughter-in-law Lady Shen hanged themselves the same day.

sentences.zh: 呂維祺，字介孺，新安人。

translations.literal: Lu Weiqi, courtesy name Jieru, was a native of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Weiqi, styled Jieru, came from Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 祖母牛氏以守節被旌。

translations.literal: His grandmother the Lady Niu was honored for preserving her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother Lady Niu was honored for her widowhood.

sentences.zh: 父孔學，事母孝，捐粟千二百石振饑，兩旌孝義。

translations.literal: His father Kongxue was filial to his mother, donated twelve hundred shi of grain to relieve famine, and was twice honored for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kongxue was filial, gave twelve hundred shi of grain in famine relief, and was twice honored for virtue.

sentences.zh: 維祺舉萬歷四十一年進士，授兗州推官，擢吏部主事，更歷四司。

translations.literal: Weiqi became jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli, was appointed investigating censor at Yanzhou, was raised to a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and served in all four bureaus in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi took the jinshi in Wanli 41, served as Yanzhou investigating censor, rose to a Personnel clerk, and rotated through all four bureaus.

sentences.zh: 光宗崩，皇長子未踐阼，內侍導幸小南城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong died the heir apparent had not yet taken the throne, and inner attendants guided him to visit the Small Southern City.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong died the heir had not yet ascended, and inner attendants led him to the Small Southern City.

sentences.zh: 維祺謁見慈慶宮，言梓宮在殯，乘輿不得輕動，乃止。

translations.literal: Weiqi paid his respects at Ciqing Palace and said that with the imperial coffin still in mourning the imperial carriage must not move lightly; the visit was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi visited Ciqing Palace and said the imperial coffin was still in mourning and the carriage must not move; the visit was canceled.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，歷考功、文選員外郎，進驗封郎中，告歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he served in turn as an officer in the Bureau of Evaluations and Appointments, was promoted to director in the Bureau of Seals, and asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he rose through Evaluations and Appointments to director in the Bureau of Seals, then retired.

sentences.zh: 開封建魏忠賢生祠，遺書士大夫戒勿預。

translations.literal: Kaifeng built a living shrine to Wei Zhongxian; he wrote to the scholar-officials warning them not to take part.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaifeng built a shrine to Wei Zhongxian, he warned scholars not to take part.

sentences.zh: 忠賢毀天下書院，維祺立芝泉講會，祀伊洛七賢。

translations.literal: Zhongxian destroyed academies throughout the realm; Weiqi founded the Zhi Spring lecture society and sacrificed to the seven sages of the Yi and Luo schools.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian destroyed academies nationwide, Weiqi founded the Zhi Spring lecture society and honored the seven Yi-Luo sages.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢南京戶部右侍郎，總督糧儲。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue and made Grand Coordinator of grain storage.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he became Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Coordinator of grain storage.

sentences.zh: 設會計簿，鉤考隱沒侵欺，及積逋不輸，各數十百萬，大者彈奏，小者捕治。

translations.literal: He set up account books, investigated concealed fraud and long arrears unpaid, each amounting to millions; major cases were impeached, minor ones arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: He set up ledgers, uncovered concealed fraud and arrears worth millions, impeached major offenders, and arrested minor ones.

sentences.zh: 立法嚴督屯課，倉庾漸充。

translations.literal: He enacted laws to supervise garrison land taxes strictly, and the granaries gradually filled.
translations.idiomatic: Strict laws on garrison land taxes gradually filled the granaries.

sentences.zh: 條上六議，曰稽出入以杜侵漁，增比較以完積案，設本科以重題覆，時會計以核支收，定差序以杜營私，禁差假以修職業。

translations.literal: He submitted six proposals in articles: audit receipts and disbursements to stop embezzlement; increase comparisons to clear backlogs; establish a reviewing bureau to weight re-examination; hold regular accounts to check payments; fix ranks of assignment to stop private dealing; forbid leave abuse to restore duty.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed six reforms: audit receipts and payments against embezzlement; tighten comparisons to clear backlogs; strengthen review; hold regular accounts; fix assignment ranks against private dealing; and curb leave abuse.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，即行之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised them and put them into practice at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and put them into effect at once.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜南京兵部尚書，參贊機務。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Nanjing Minister of War and participated in deliberating on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he became Nanjing Minister of War and joined in military deliberations.

sentences.zh: 清冒伍八千余名。

translations.literal: He cleared more than eight thousand falsely enrolled soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He struck more than eight thousand falsely enrolled soldiers from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 請申飭江防，鳳陵單外為憂，弗省。

translations.literal: He asked that the Yangzi defenses be tightened, warning that Fengyang's imperial tombs lay exposed; the warning was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He urged tighter Yangzi defenses, warning that the imperial tombs at Fengyang lay exposed, but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，賊犯江北，遣參將薛邦臣防全椒，趙世臣戍浦口。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year bandits invaded the north bank of the Yangzi; he sent Vice Commander Xue Bangchen to defend Quanjiao and Zhao Shichen to garrison Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year eight rebels struck north of the Yangzi; he sent Xue Bangchen to Quanjiao and Zhao Shichen to Pukou.

sentences.zh: 世臣潰走，南京震動，鳳陽亦旋告陷。

translations.literal: Shichen fled in rout; Nanjing was shaken, and Fengyang soon reported its fall.
translations.idiomatic: Shichen fled in rout, Nanjing was shaken, and Fengyang soon fell.

sentences.zh: 大計拾遺，言官復劾他事，遂除名。

translations.literal: At the grand evaluation he was listed among omissions; censors impeached him on other matters, and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand evaluation censors impeached him on other grounds and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時維祺父孔學避賊洛陽，維祺乃歸留洛，立伊洛會，及門二百余人。

translations.literal: At that time Weiqi's father Kongxue had fled the bandits to Luoyang; Weiqi returned and stayed in Luoyang, founded the Yi-Luo society, and had more than two hundred disciples.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kongxue had fled to Luoyang; Weiqi stayed there, founded the Yi-Luo society, and gathered more than two hundred disciples.

sentences.zh: 著《孝經本義》成，上之。

translations.literal: He completed his Original Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He finished his Original Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十二年，洛陽大饑。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Luoyang suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve Luoyang suffered severe famine.

sentences.zh: 維祺勸福王常洵散財餉士，以振人心，王不省。

translations.literal: Weiqi urged the Prince of Fu, Changxun, to distribute wealth to feed the troops and steady hearts; the prince did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi urged Prince Changxun of Fu to spend his wealth feeding troops and steadying morale; the prince ignored him.

sentences.zh: 乃盡出私廩，設局振濟。

translations.literal: He then emptied his private granaries and set up relief offices.
translations.idiomatic: He emptied his private granaries and set up relief offices.

sentences.zh: 事聞，復官。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 然饑民多從賊者，河南賊復大熾。

translations.literal: Yet many of the starving joined the bandits, and the rebels in Henan flared up again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many starving people joined the rebels, and Henan flared up again.

sentences.zh: 無何，李自成大舉來攻，維祺分守洛陽北城。

translations.literal: Before long Li Zicheng came in force to attack; Weiqi was assigned to defend Luoyang's north wall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Zicheng attacked in force; Weiqi was assigned the north wall of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 夜半，總兵王紹禹之軍有騎而馳者，周呼於城上，城外亦呼而應之，於是城陷。

translations.literal: At midnight in the army of the commander Wang Shaoyu horsemen were seen riding out; calls went around on the wall, answered from outside, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight horsemen rode out from Wang Shaoyu's army; calls on the wall were answered from outside, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 賊有識維祺者曰：「子非振饑呂尚書乎？

translations.literal: A bandit who knew Weiqi said: "Are you not Minister Lu who relieved famine?
translations.idiomatic: A rebel who knew him said, "Are you not Minister Lu who fed the starving?

sentences.zh: 我能活爾，爾可以間去。」

translations.literal: I can spare your life—you may slip away in the confusion."
translations.idiomatic: I can spare you—you may slip away in the confusion."

sentences.zh: 維祺弗應，賊擁維祺去。

translations.literal: Weiqi did not answer; the bandits dragged him away.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi did not answer; the rebels dragged him away.

sentences.zh: 時福王常洵匿民舍中，賊跡而執之，遇維祺於道。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Fu, Changxun, was hiding in a commoner's house; the bandits tracked him down and seized him, meeting Weiqi on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changxun of Fu was hiding in a commoner's house; the rebels tracked him down and met Weiqi on the road.

sentences.zh: 維祺反接，望見王，呼曰：「王，綱常至重。

translations.literal: Weiqi, hands bound behind him, saw the prince and cried: "Your Highness, the bonds of propriety are paramount.
translations.idiomatic: Bound, Weiqi saw the prince and cried, "Your Highness, ritual propriety is everything.

sentences.zh: 等死耳，毋屈膝於賊！」

translations.literal: Death is the same in any case—do not kneel to bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Death is the same—do not kneel to rebels!"

sentences.zh: 王瞠不語。

translations.literal: The prince stared and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The prince stared and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 見賊渠於周公廟，按其項使跪，不屈，延頸就刃而死。

translations.literal: Brought before the bandit chief at the Temple of the Duke of Zhou, they pressed his neck to make him kneel; he would not yield and stretched his neck to the blade and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the Temple of the Duke of Zhou they forced him to kneel; he refused, stretched his neck to the blade, and died.

sentences.zh: 時十四年之正月某日也。

translations.literal: It was a certain day in the first month of the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: It was a day in the first month of year fourteen.

sentences.zh: 維祺年五十有五，贈太子少保，祭葬，蔭子如制。

translations.literal: Weiqi was fifty-five; he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granted sacrificial burial, and his sons given hereditary privilege according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi was fifty-five; he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, given state burial, and his sons hereditary honors as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 而維祺之家在新安者，十六年城陷，家亦破。

translations.literal: But Weiqi's family home in Xin'an, when the city fell in the sixteenth year, was also destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: His family home in Xin'an was destroyed when that city fell in year sixteen.

sentences.zh: 弟維祮，字泰孺，由選貢生為樂平知縣者也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Weineng, courtesy name Tairu, had entered office through the selected tribute student route and become magistrate of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Weineng, styled Tairu, had become magistrate of Leping through the tribute-student route.

sentences.zh: 至是解職歸，亦抗節死。

translations.literal: By then he had left office and returned home, and also died resisting to the end.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had retired home and also died defiantly.

sentences.zh: 贈按察僉事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Commissioner of Surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 福王立南京，加贈維祺太傅，謚忠節。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu established his court at Nanjing, Weiqi was further posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu ruled from Nanjing, Weiqi was further made Grand Tutor posthumously and titled Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 王家禎，長垣人。

translations.literal: Wang Jiazhen was a native of Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiazhen came from Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年進士。

translations.literal: He became jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Wanli 35.

sentences.zh: 天啟間，歷官左僉都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he served in succession as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 松山部長銀定、歹成擾西鄙二十余年，家禎至，三犯三卻之，先後斬首五百四十。

translations.literal: The Songshan chieftains Yinding and Daicheng had disturbed the western borderlands for more than twenty years; when Jiazhen arrived he repelled them three times in three invasions and in all beheaded five hundred and forty.
translations.idiomatic: The Songshan chiefs Yinding and Daicheng had raided the west for twenty years; Jiazhen repelled three invasions and beheaded five hundred and forty in all.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部右侍郎，轉左。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Minister of Revenue and then transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Revenue, then to the left-hand post.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年攝部事，邊餉不以時發。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he acted as head of the ministry, but frontier pay was not issued on time.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he acted as head of the ministry, but frontier pay was not issued on time.

sentences.zh: 秋，遼東兵鼓噪，巡撫畢自肅自縊死。

translations.literal: In autumn the Liaodong troops mutinied; Grand Coordinator Bi Zisu hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Liaodong troops mutinied; Grand Coordinator Bi Zisu hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，削家禎籍。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and struck Jiazhen from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and struck Jiazhen from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 已，敘甘肅功，復其冠帶。

translations.literal: Later, recounting his Gansu merit, his cap and belt were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later his Gansu merit was recognized and his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，京師被兵，起兵部左侍郎，尋以本官兼右僉都御史，總理河南、湖廣、山西、陜西、四川、江北軍務，代盧象升討賊。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year, when the capital region was under attack, he was made Left Vice Minister of War; soon with that rank he was also made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to oversee military affairs in Henan, Huguang, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Jiangbei, replacing Lu Xiangsheng in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year nine, with the capital threatened, he became Left Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief overseeing Henan, Huguang, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Jiangbei, replacing Lu Xiangsheng against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 會河南巡撫陳必謙罷，即命兼之。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Chen Biqian of Henan was dismissed, he was ordered to hold that post as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan Grand Coordinator Chen Biqian was dismissed, he was ordered to hold that post as well.

sentences.zh: 督將士會剿賊馬進忠等於南陽，復遣兵救襄陽，大戰牌樓閣。

translations.literal: He directed officers and soldiers in a joint campaign against the bandits Ma Jinzhong and others at Nanyang, and also sent troops to relieve Xiangyang, fighting a great battle at Pailou Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops against Ma Jinzhong at Nanyang, sent relief to Xiangyang, and fought a great battle at Pailou Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 其冬，家丁鼓噪，燒開封西門。

translations.literal: That winter his household retainers mutinied and burned Kaifeng's west gate.
translations.idiomatic: That winter his household troops mutinied and burned Kaifeng's west gate.

sentences.zh: 家禎夜自外歸，慰諭犒賞，詰旦，發往南陽討土寇楊四以去。

translations.literal: Jiazhen returned from outside at night, comforted them with rewards, and at dawn set out for Nanyang to suppress the local bandit Yang Si.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen returned at night, calmed them with rewards, and at dawn marched to Nanyang against the local bandit Yang Si.

sentences.zh: 楊四者，舞陽劇盜也。

translations.literal: Yang Si was a fierce bandit of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Si was a fierce bandit of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 初，四與其黨郭三海、侯馭民等降於必謙，至是復叛，故家禎有是遣。

translations.literal: Earlier Si and his followers Guo Sanhai, Hou Yumin, and others had surrendered to Biqian; now they rebelled again, hence Jiazhen's dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Si and his followers Guo Sanhai and Hou Yumin had once surrendered to Biqian but rebelled again, hence Jiazhen's march.

sentences.zh: 其後南陽同知萬年策與監紀推官湯開遠，諸將左良玉、牟文綬等連破四，四焚死，其黨亦為諸將所擒誅雲。

translations.literal: Afterward Nanyang Vice Prefect Wan Niance and supervising secretary Tang Kaiyuan, with the generals Zuo Liangyu, Mou Wenshou, and others, repeatedly defeated Si; Si burned to death, and his followers were also captured and executed by the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wan Niance, Tang Kaiyuan, and generals Zuo Liangyu and Mou Wenshou repeatedly defeated him; Si burned to death and his followers were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 當是時，流賊盡趨江北，留都震驚。

translations.literal: At that time the roving bandits all pressed toward the north bank of the Yangzi, and the southern capital was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebels had all pressed toward the Yangzi's north bank, and Nanjing was shaken.

sentences.zh: 言者謂家禎奉命討安慶賊，未嘗一出中州。

translations.literal: Critics said Jiazhen had been ordered to suppress bandits at Anqing and had never once left the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said he had been ordered to fight Anqing rebels but had never left the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以家丁之變心輕之。

translations.literal: The emperor also took him lightly because of the household mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also lost confidence in him after the household mutiny.

sentences.zh: 明年四月乃以總理授熊文燦，令家禎專撫河南。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year the post of supreme coordinator was given to Xiong Wencan, and Jiazhen was ordered to concentrate on governing Henan as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: The next fourth month Xiong Wencan was made supreme coordinator, and Jiazhen was left to govern Henan alone.

sentences.zh: 文燦未至，詔遣左良玉援安慶，家禎不遣。

translations.literal: Wencan had not yet arrived; an edict ordered Zuo Liangyu to relieve Anqing, but Jiazhen did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wencan arrived, the court ordered Zuo Liangyu to relieve Anqing, but Jiazhen did not send him.

sentences.zh: 秋，劉國能犯開封，裨將李春貴等戰歿。

translations.literal: In autumn Liu Guoneng attacked Kaifeng; the lieutenant generals Li Chungui and others died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Liu Guoneng attacked Kaifeng; Lieutenant Generals Li Chungui and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 議罪，家禎落職閑住。

translations.literal: His guilt was debated and Jiazhen was dismissed to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Blame was debated and Jiazhen was dismissed to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 久之，李自成陷京師，遣兵據長垣，設偽官。

translations.literal: After a long while Li Zicheng took the capital, sent troops to occupy Changyuan, and set up false officials.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Li Zicheng took the capital, seized Changyuan, and set up puppet officials.

sentences.zh: 家禎與其子元炌並自經死。

translations.literal: Jiazhen and his son Yuanchao both hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen and his son Yuanchao hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 焦源溥，字涵一，三原人。

translations.literal: Jiao Yuanpu, courtesy name Hanyi, was a native of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Yuanpu, styled Hanyi, came from Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He became jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Wanli 41.

sentences.zh: 歷知沙河、浚二縣，考最，召為御史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Shahe and Jun counties; rated highest in evaluation, he was summoned as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Shahe and Jun, rated highest, and was summoned as a censor.

sentences.zh: 熹宗嗣位，移宮議起，刑部尚書黃克纘請寬盜寶諸奄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong succeeded, the debate over moving the palace arose; Minister of Justice Huang Keguan asked leniency for the eunuchs who had stolen imperial treasures.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong succeeded, the palace-move controversy erupted; Minister of Justice Huang Keguan urged leniency for the treasure-stealing eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 源溥折之曰：「光宗，神宗元子也；

translations.literal: Yuanpu refuted him, saying: "Emperor Guangzong was the eldest son of Emperor Shenzong;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanpu rebutted him: "Guangzong was Shenzong's eldest son—

sentences.zh: 為元子者為忠，則為福藩者非忠。

translations.literal: to side with the eldest son is loyalty, then to side with the Prince of Fu is disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: loyalty lies with the eldest son; siding with the Prince of Fu is disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 孝端、孝靖，神宗後也；

translations.literal: Empresses Xiaoduan and Xiaojing were consorts of Shenzong;
translations.idiomatic: Empresses Xiaoduan and Xiaojing were Shenzong's consorts—

sentences.zh: 為二後者為忠，則為鄭貴妃者非忠。

translations.literal: to side with the two empresses is loyalty, then to side with Consort Zheng is disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: loyalty lies with the two empresses; siding with Consort Zheng is disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 孝元、孝和，光宗後也；

translations.literal: Empresses Xiaoyuan and Xiaohe were consorts of Guangzong;
translations.idiomatic: Empresses Xiaoyuan and Xiaohe were Guangzong's consorts—

sentences.zh: 為二後者為忠，則為李選侍者非忠。

translations.literal: to side with the two empresses is loyalty, then to side with Attendant Li is disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: loyalty lies with the two empresses; siding with Attendant Li is disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 貴妃三十年心事，人誰不知？

translations.literal: The consort's thirty years of designs—who does not know them?
translations.idiomatic: Who did not know the consort's thirty years of designs?

sentences.zh: 張差持梃，危在呼吸，尚忍言哉！

translations.literal: Zhang Chai wielded a club; danger hung by a breath—how can one still speak of leniency!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai raised a club and death hung by a breath—how can one still plead leniency!

sentences.zh: 況當先帝御極之初，忽傳皇祖封後之命，請封不得，冶容進矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of the late emperor's reign, there suddenly came word of the imperial grandfather's command to make her empress; when the request was denied, she advanced with alluring looks.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the late emperor's reign came word of a command to make her empress; denied, she advanced with seductive looks.

sentences.zh: 張差之梃不中，則投以女優之惑；

translations.literal: When Zhang Chai's club missed its mark, female entertainers were sent to beguile him;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chai's club missed, female entertainers were sent to beguile him;

sentences.zh: 崔文升之藥不速，則促以李可灼之丸。

translations.literal: when Cui Wensheng's medicine did not act quickly enough, Li Kezhuo's pills were pressed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: when Cui Wensheng's medicine was too slow, Li Kezhuo's pills were pressed upon him.

sentences.zh: 痛哉！

translations.literal: How painful!
translations.idiomatic: How painful!

sentences.zh: 先帝欲諱言進禦之事，遂甘蒙不白之冤。

translations.literal: The late emperor wished to hush talk of what entered the imperial bedchamber, and so willingly bore an unredressed injustice.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor wished to hush what entered the bedchamber and bore an unredressed injustice.

sentences.zh: 今即厚待貴妃，始終恩禮，而鄭養性之都督不可不奪也，崔文升不可不磔也。

translations.literal: Even if the consort is now treated generously with enduring favor, Zheng Yangxing's commandery must not be left intact, and Cui Wensheng must be dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the consort is now treated generously, Zheng Yangxing's command must be stripped and Cui Wensheng dismembered.

sentences.zh: 若竟置弗問，不幾於忘父乎！

translations.literal: If they are left altogether unpunished, is that not nearly forgetting one's father!
translations.idiomatic: To leave them unpunished is nearly to forget one's father!

sentences.zh: 李選侍一宮人，更非貴妃比，如聖諭阻陛下於暖閣，挾陛下以垂簾，及淩虐聖母狀，有臣子所不忍言者。

translations.literal: Attendant Li was only a palace woman, far beneath a consort; as the sacred edict said, she blocked Your Majesty in the warm chamber, held Your Majesty to rule from behind the curtain, and abused the empress mother—things a subject cannot bear to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Li was only a palace woman, far beneath a consort; she blocked Your Majesty in the warm chamber, held you to rule from behind the curtain, and abused the empress mother—things subjects cannot bear to recount.

sentences.zh: 今即為選侍乞憐，第可求曲宥前辜，量從優典，而移宮始末不可得而抹摋也，盜寶諸奄不可得而寬宥也。

translations.literal: Even if one now pleads pity for Attendant Li, one may only ask indulgence for past offenses and measured favor; the whole course of moving the palace cannot be erased, nor can the treasure-stealing eunuchs be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one pleads for Attendant Li, only past offenses may be indulged; the palace move cannot be erased, nor the treasure-stealing eunuchs pardoned.

sentences.zh: 若竟置諸奄弗問，不幾於忘母乎！」

translations.literal: If the eunuchs are left altogether unpunished, is that not nearly forgetting one's mother!"
translations.idiomatic: To leave the eunuchs unpunished is nearly to forget one's mother!"

sentences.zh: 疏上，舉朝寒懼。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the whole court shuddered in fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial went up, the whole court shuddered.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年憂歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he returned home in mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋還朝，出按真定諸府，例轉鳳陽兵備副使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned to court, went out to inspect the prefectures of Zhending, and by regulation was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned, inspected Zhending prefectures, and was transferred to Fengyang military vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時崔文升出鎮兩淮，欲甘心源溥，遂移疾歸。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Wensheng was posted to command the two Huai regions and wished to ruin Yuanpu; Yuanpu therefore pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wensheng was then posted to the two Huai regions and meant to ruin him; Yuanpu pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年起故官，分巡河東道，遷寧武參政，有平寇功，就遷山西按察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former office, toured the Hedong circuit, was transferred to Pacification Commissioner at Ningwu, had merit in suppressing bandits, and was then made Shanxi Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 he was recalled, toured Hedong, became Ningwu Pacification Commissioner, suppressed bandits, and rose to Shanxi Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年擢右僉都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 時邊事日棘，兵缺伍，餉又久乏，歲洊饑，民淘馬糞以食。

translations.literal: At that time frontier affairs grew daily more urgent; troops lacked full rolls, pay had long been short, famine came year after year, and the people sifted horse dung for food.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier affairs grew urgent; troops were understrength, pay long overdue, famine repeated yearly, and people sifted horse dung for food.

sentences.zh: 源溥請蠲振增餉，當事不能應。

translations.literal: Yuanpu asked for tax remission, relief grain, and increased pay, but those in charge could not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanpu asked for tax relief, grain aid, and higher pay, but the authorities could not comply.

sentences.zh: 逾年，自劾求去，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year he impeached himself and asked to leave; he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he impeached himself and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，李自成陷關中，與從兄源清同被執，勒令輸金。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year Li Zicheng took Guanzhong; he and his elder cousin Yuanqing were seized together and ordered to pay gold.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year sixteen Li Zicheng took Guanzhong; he and his cousin Yuanqing were seized and ordered to pay gold.

sentences.zh: 源溥瞋目大罵，賊拔其舌，支解之。

translations.literal: Yuanpu glared and cursed loudly; the bandits cut out his tongue and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanpu glared and cursed; the rebels cut out his tongue and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 源清，字湛一，由進士歷官宣府巡撫。

translations.literal: Yuanqing, courtesy name Zhanyi, entered through the jinshi route and rose in office to Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing, styled Zhanyi, rose through the jinshi route to Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，坐萬全左衛失守，奪官謫戍。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year, because Wanquan Left Guard fell, he was stripped of office and banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year seven Wanquan Left Guard fell; he was stripped of office and banished.

sentences.zh: 久之釋還，年七十。

translations.literal: After a long while he was released and returned, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was released, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 至是抗節，不食七日死。

translations.literal: By then he resisted to the end and died after seven days without food.
translations.idiomatic: By then he resisted to the end and died after seven days without food.

sentences.zh: 李夢辰，字元居，睢州人。

translations.literal: Li Mengchen, courtesy name Yuanju, was a native of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengchen, styled Yuanju, came from Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: He became jinshi in the first year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Chongzhen 1.

sentences.zh: 授庶吉士，改兵科給事中，時盜起陜西，山東曹、濮間之盜，道梗三百余裏，河北有回賊。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin bachelor, then transferred to supervising secretary in the Bureau of War; at that time bandits rose in Shaanxi, bandits between Cao and Pu in Shandong blocked the roads for more than three hundred li, and in Hebei there were Hui bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Made a Hanlin bachelor, then War Bureau supervising secretary; bandits rose in Shaanxi, blocked roads for three hundred li between Cao and Pu in Shandong, and Hui bandits appeared in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 夢辰歷陳其狀，請敕將吏急防。

translations.literal: Mengchen set forth the situation in detail and asked that generals and officials be urgently ordered to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Mengchen detailed the situation and urged urgent orders to generals and officials to guard against them.

sentences.zh: 五年，上疏言：「中外交訌，秦、晉、齊、魯多亂，兩河居中尤要地。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he submitted a memorial saying: "Within and without there is strife; Qin, Jin, Qi, and Lu are mostly in disorder, and the two river provinces at the center are especially crucial.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he memorialized: "Strife within and without has thrown Qin, Jin, Qi, and Lu into disorder, and the two central river provinces are especially crucial.

sentences.zh: 鉛硝久市直未償，漕米歲輸累無已，宗祿並征，南陽加派，河決歲歉，郵傳催科之患百出，民室如懸罄，生計日不支，急難誰肯用命？

translations.literal: Lead and saltpeter prices in the capital market long unpaid, transport grain levied year after year without end, princely stipends collected together, extra levies in Nanyang, river breaches and yearly crop failure, the hundred afflictions of courier service and tax collection—the people's stores are as if emptied, livelihoods daily cannot be sustained; in sudden crisis who will obey orders?
translations.idiomatic: Unpaid lead and saltpeter debts, endless transport grain levies, princely stipends collected together, extra Nanyang levies, river breaches and crop failure, courier and tax abuses everywhere—households emptied, livelihoods failing; who will obey in crisis?

sentences.zh: 兩河標兵、磁兵，新舊不滿七千，一有警，防禦何資？

translations.literal: The two river provinces' standard troops and Ci troops, old and new together fewer than seven thousand—once alarm comes, with what shall defense be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: The two provinces' standard and Ci troops number fewer than seven thousand—what defense is possible once alarm comes?

sentences.zh: 今日之務急防河，繕城，備器，練鄉兵，治甲胄，尤以收拾人心為本。」

translations.literal: Today's tasks are urgently to defend the river, repair walls, prepare weapons, train local militia, restore armor, and above all to rally popular hearts as the foundation."
translations.idiomatic: Today's tasks are to defend the river, repair walls, prepare arms, train militia, restore armor, and above all rally the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 帝命所司嚴飭。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to enforce this strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to enforce this strictly.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，鉅盜盡萃河北。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year the great bandits all gathered in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the great bandits all gathered in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 夢辰慮其南犯，請敕河南諸道監司急防渡口，而巡撫移駐衛輝，與山西、保定二撫臣掎角急擊。

translations.literal: Mengchen feared they would invade south and asked that Henan's circuit supervisors urgently guard the crossings; the grand coordinator should move his headquarters to Weihui and, with the coordinators of Shanxi and Baoding, strike in pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a southern invasion, he urged Henan supervisors to guard the crossings, the grand coordinator to move to Weihui, and Shanxi and Baoding coordinators to strike in concert.

sentences.zh: 帝方下兵部議，賊已從澠池潛渡。

translations.literal: The emperor had just referred the matter to the Ministry of War for discussion when the bandits had already secretly crossed from Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just referred the matter to the Ministry of War when the bandits had already crossed secretly from Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 自是中州郡縣無日不告警矣。

translations.literal: From then on the prefectures and counties of the Central Plain were not a day without alarm.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Central Plain was alarmed every day.

sentences.zh: 累遷本科左給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Supervising Secretary of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Supervising Secretary of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 復言：「將驕軍悍，鄧玘、張外嘉之兵弒主而叛，曹文詔、艾萬年之兵望賊而奔，尤世威、徐來朝之兵離汛而遁，今者，張全昌、趙光遠之兵且倒戈為亂矣。

translations.literal: He spoke again: "Generals are arrogant and troops fierce; the armies of Deng Qi and Zhang Waijia murdered their commanders and rebelled; the armies of Cao Wenzhao and Ai Wannian fled at sight of bandits; the armies of You Shiwei and Xu Laichao left their posts and ran; now the armies of Zhang Quanchang and Zhao Guangyuan have turned their spears in mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: He said again: "Generals are arrogant and troops fierce—Deng Qi and Zhang Waijia's men murdered their commanders; Cao Wenzhao and Ai Wannian's men fled at sight of bandits; You Shiwei and Xu Laichao's men deserted their posts; now Zhang Quanchang and Zhao Guangyuan's men have mutinied.

sentences.zh: 滎澤劫庫殺人，偃師列營對壘。

translations.literal: At Xingyang they raided the treasury and killed men; at Yanshi they pitched camps facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyang they raided the treasury and killed men; at Yanshi they faced one another in camp.

sentences.zh: 且全昌等會剿豫賊，隨處逗遛，及中途兵變，全昌竟東行，光遠始西向。

translations.literal: Moreover Quanchang and others joined in suppressing Henan bandits but dallied everywhere; when mutiny broke out midway, Quanchang went east while Guangyuan only then turned west.
translations.idiomatic: Quanchang and others dallied everywhere on the Henan campaign; when mutiny broke out midway, Quanchang went east while Guangyuan only then turned west.

sentences.zh: 驕抗如此，安可不重治。」

translations.literal: Such arrogance and defiance—how can they not be severely punished?"
translations.idiomatic: Such arrogance—how can they escape severe punishment?"

sentences.zh: 帝頗采其言。

translations.literal: The emperor largely adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 進吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 都御史唐世濟薦霍維華，福建巡按應喜臣薦周維京，冀並翻逆案。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Tang Shiji recommended Huo Weihua, and Fujian touring censor Ying Xichen recommended Zhou Weijing, hoping together to overturn the treason cases.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Tang Shiji recommended Huo Weihua and Fujian censor Ying Xichen recommended Zhou Weijing, hoping to overturn the treason cases.

sentences.zh: 夢辰疏駁之，世濟、喜臣皆下吏謫戍。

translations.literal: Mengchen memorialized in rebuttal; Shiji and Xichen were both sent to the magistrates and banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Mengchen rebutted them in a memorial; Shiji and Xichen were prosecuted and banished.

sentences.zh: 尋擢太常少卿，累遷至通政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and rose in succession to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and rose to Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 坐代人削章奏，貶秩調任。

translations.literal: Because he had another person trim a memorial for him, he was demoted in rank and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Because another person had trimmed a memorial for him, he was demoted and transferred.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有持金囑中書舍人某賄大學士，求為副都御史者。

translations.literal: Before long someone brought gold and asked a certain Secretariat drafter to bribe a grand secretary to obtain the post of Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone brought gold and asked a Secretariat drafter to bribe a grand secretary for the post of Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 邏卒廉得之，詞連夢辰。

translations.literal: Patrol guards discovered it through investigation, and the testimony implicated Mengchen.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol guards uncovered it, and the testimony implicated Mengchen.

sentences.zh: 帝令夢辰自奏，事得白。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Mengchen to report on himself, and the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Mengchen to report on himself, and he was cleared.

sentences.zh: 然夢辰竟坐是削籍。

translations.literal: Yet Mengchen was still struck from the rolls on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Mengchen was still struck from the rolls over the affair.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，賊攻開封，不克，遂去，陷西華，屠陳州，逼睢州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year the bandits attacked Kaifeng but could not take it, then departed, took Xihua, massacred Chenzhou, and pressed Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year fifteen the rebels failed at Kaifeng, took Xihua, massacred Chenzhou, and pressed Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 時州缺正官，夢辰歸，即乘城主守。

translations.literal: The prefecture then lacked a regular magistrate; Mengchen had returned home and at once mounted the wall to command the defense.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lacked a magistrate; Mengchen had returned home and at once took command on the wall.

sentences.zh: 無何，賊從他門入，擁夢辰見羅汝才。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits entered by another gate and brought Mengchen before Luo Rucai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels entered by another gate and brought Mengchen before Luo Rucai.

sentences.zh: 汝才問所欲，曰：「我大臣，但欲死爾。」

translations.literal: Rucai asked what he wanted; he said: "I am a great minister—I only wish to die."
translations.idiomatic: Rucai asked what he wanted; he said, "I am a great minister—I only wish to die."

sentences.zh: 汝才去，遣其客說降，且進之酒。

translations.literal: Rucai left, sent a guest to urge surrender, and offered him wine.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai left, sent a guest to urge surrender, and offered wine.

sentences.zh: 夢辰覆杯於地，太息起，扼吭而卒。

translations.literal: Mengchen overturned the cup on the ground, sighed deeply, rose, and died clutching his throat.
translations.idiomatic: Mengchen overturned the cup, sighed, rose, and died clutching his throat.

sentences.zh: 妻王氏，方病，聞之，不食死。

translations.literal: His wife the Lady Wang was ill; on hearing it she died without eating.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Wang, ill, died without eating on hearing it.

sentences.zh: 宋師襄，耀州人。

translations.literal: Song Shixiang was a native of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shixiang came from Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He became jinshi in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Wanli 44.

sentences.zh: 歷官御史。

translations.literal: He served in office as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年五月請罷內操，言：「自劉朝營脫死，與沈纮謀為固寵計。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Tianqi he asked that inner-court drilling be abolished, saying: "Since Liu Chao escaped death from camp, he and Shen Hong plotted to secure favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianqi 3 he asked to abolish inner-court drilling, saying, "Since Liu Chao escaped death in camp, he and Shen Hong plotted to secure favor.

sentences.zh: 纮以募兵為朝外護，朝以內操為纮內援。

translations.literal: Hong used recruited troops as Chao's outer support, and Chao used inner drilling as Hong's inner support.
translations.idiomatic: Hong used recruited troops as Chao's outer support, and Chao used inner drilling as Hong's inner support.

sentences.zh: 宮府內外，知有朝而不知天子。

translations.literal: Within and without the palace they knew Chao but not the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the palace they knew Chao but not the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天牖聖聰，一旦發露，屏之南京。

translations.literal: Heaven enlightened the sage ear; once exposed, Chao was banished to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven enlightened the emperor; once exposed, Chao was banished to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 然朝雖去，而三千虎旅安歸？

translations.literal: Yet though Chao is gone, where shall his three thousand tiger troops go?
translations.idiomatic: Yet though Chao is gone, where shall his three thousand tiger troops go?

sentences.zh: 世未有蓄怨藏怒之人潛布左右而不為患者，今惟有散之而已。

translations.literal: Never in the world has one who harbors hidden wrath been posted at one's side without causing harm; now there is only to disperse them.
translations.idiomatic: Never has one who harbors hidden wrath been posted at one's side without harm; they must be dispersed.

sentences.zh: 夫平日卵翼朝者，黃克纘也，亡何以戎政內宣；

translations.literal: He who daily sheltered Chao was Huang Keguan—why is military administration now proclaimed within the palace?
translations.idiomatic: Huang Keguan daily sheltered Chao—why is military administration now proclaimed within the palace?

sentences.zh: 抄參朝者，毛士龍也，未幾以構陷削籍。

translations.literal: He who copied and reported on Chao was Mao Shilong; before long he was struck from the rolls on a framed charge.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Shilong copied and reported on Chao; soon he was struck from the rolls on a framed charge.

sentences.zh: 豈非握兵據要，轉相恐喝，以至是乎？」

translations.literal: Is it not because they hold troops and key posts and intimidate one another, leading to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Is it not because they hold troops and key posts and intimidate one another?"

sentences.zh: 帝以內操祖宗故事，不納。

translations.literal: The emperor, citing inner drilling as an ancestral precedent, did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, citing ancestral precedent, did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 又陳足財之策，請減上供，汰冗官，核營造，省賚賞。

translations.literal: He also set forth measures to secure sufficient funds, asking to reduce tribute to the throne, cut redundant offices, audit construction, and reduce gifts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed securing funds by reducing tribute, cutting redundant offices, auditing construction, and reducing gifts and rewards.

sentences.zh: 皆宦官所不便，格不行。

translations.literal: All were inconvenient to the eunuchs and were blocked from implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were inconvenient to the eunuchs and were blocked.

sentences.zh: 奉聖夫人客氏子及中官王體乾、宋晉、魏進忠等十二人俱世襲錦衣。
