translations.literal: The son of the Lady of Imperial Favor Ke and the palace eunuchs Wang Tigan, Song Jin, Wei Jinzhong, and twelve others in all were all granted hereditary posts in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The son of Lady Ke of Imperial Favor and twelve palace eunuchs including Wang Tigan, Song Jin, and Wei Jinzhong were granted hereditary Embroidered-Uniform Guard posts.

sentences.zh: 進忠者，魏忠賢也。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong was Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 師襄力諫。

translations.literal: Shixiang remonstrated strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiang remonstrated strenuously.

sentences.zh: 又言左都御史熊尚文、工部侍郎周應秋、登萊巡撫袁可立當去不去，光祿卿須之彥、太常卿呂純如不當來而來。

translations.literal: He also said that Left Censor-in-Chief Xiong Shangwen, Vice Minister of Works Zhou Yingqiu, and Grand Coordinator of Deng-Lai Yuan Keli ought to leave but had not, while Minister of Imperial Entertainments Xu Zhiyan and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Lü Chunru ought not to come but had come.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Xiong Shangwen, Zhou Yingqiu, and Yuan Keli ought to leave but had not, while Xu Zhiyan and Lü Chunru ought not to come but had.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor heard none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard none of it.

sentences.zh: 四年，巡按河南。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he toured and inspected Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he toured Henan as censor.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，言：「今之言者，皆曰治平要務，乃終日籌邊事、商國計、飭吏治、計民生、弭盜賊，而漫無實效。

translations.literal: On taking leave at court he said: "Today's speakers all call these the essentials of good government, yet they spend their days planning frontier affairs, discussing state finance, tightening official discipline, reckoning the people's livelihood, and suppressing bandits, with no real effect at all.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave he said, "Today's speakers all call these the essentials of good government, yet they spend their days on frontier affairs, state finance, official discipline, livelihood, and bandits—with no real effect.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，臺諫以進言為責，條奏一入，即雲盡職，言之行否，置弗問矣。

translations.literal: The reason is that the censorate and remonstrance bureaus take submitting words as their duty; once a memorial enters, they at once say they have done their office, and whether the words are carried out is left unasked.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that censors take submitting words as their duty; once a memorial enters, they say their office is done, and whether it is carried out is left unasked.

sentences.zh: 六曹以題覆為責，題覆一上，即雲畢事，事之行否，置弗問矣。

translations.literal: The six ministries took submitting review reports as their duty; once a review went up, they at once said the matter was finished, and whether it was carried out was left unasked.
translations.idiomatic: The six ministries treated review reports as their duty; once a report went up, they called the matter finished and never asked whether it was carried out.

sentences.zh: 內閣以票擬為責，票擬一定，即為明綸，旨之行否，置弗問矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Council took drafting rescripts as its duty; once a draft was fixed, it became the clear edict, and whether the order was carried out was left unasked.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council treated drafting rescripts as its duty; once a draft was fixed, it became law, and whether the order was carried out was left unasked.

sentences.zh: 上謾下欺，釀成大患。

translations.literal: Superiors deceived and subordinates cheated, brewing great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors deceived and subordinates cheated, brewing great calamity.

sentences.zh: 今人怨已極，天怒已甚，災害並至，民不聊生，相聚思亂，十而八九。

translations.literal: Now popular resentment has reached its limit, Heaven's anger is extreme, disasters come together, the people cannot live, they gather and think of rebellion—eight or nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Popular resentment has peaked, Heaven's anger is extreme, disasters multiply, the people cannot live, and eight or nine in ten think of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 臣恐今日之患，不在遼左、黔、蜀，而在數百年休養之赤子也。」

translations.literal: Your subject fears today's peril lies not in Liaodong, Guizhou, or Sichuan, but in the common people nurtured in peace for hundreds of years."
translations.idiomatic: I fear today's peril lies not in Liaodong, Guizhou, or Sichuan, but in the common people nurtured in peace for centuries."

sentences.zh: 明年復命薦部內人才，首及尚書盛以弘。

translations.literal: The next year he was again ordered to recommend talent within the ministry, naming first Minister Sheng Yihong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again ordered to recommend ministry talent, naming Minister Sheng Yihong first.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢責以徇私，貶一秩調任，師襄遂歸。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian charged him with favoritism; he was demoted one rank and transferred, and Shixiang then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian charged favoritism; he was demoted one rank and transferred, and Shixiang went home.

sentences.zh: 麻僖，慶陽人。

translations.literal: Ma Xi was a native of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xi came from Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 父永吉，由庶吉士為御史，終湖廣按察使，以清操聞。

translations.literal: His father Yongji entered through the Hanlin bachelor route as a censor and ended as Huguang Surveillance Commissioner, famed for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yongji rose from Hanlin bachelor to censor and ended as Huguang Surveillance Commissioner, famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 僖舉萬歷三十五年進士，授庶吉士，改兵科給事中。

translations.literal: Xi became jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and transferred to supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: Xi took the jinshi in Wanli 35, became a Hanlin bachelor, and transferred to War Bureau supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 代王長子鼎渭訐父廢長立幼，僖劾代王無君鼎渭無父。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dai's eldest son Dingwei denounced his father for deposing the elder and establishing the younger; Xi impeached the prince of Dai as lacking the way of a lord and Dingwei as lacking filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dai's eldest son Dingwei denounced his father for deposing the elder heir; Xi impeached the prince as unprincely and Dingwei as unfilial.

sentences.zh: 四十年，疏陳納諫諍、舉枚卜、補大僚、登遺佚、速考選數事，不報。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he memorialized on accepting remonstrance, holding divination for high appointments, filling great offices, elevating the overlooked, and speeding examinations and selections—no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty he memorialized on accepting remonstrance, holding divination for appointments, filling high offices, elevating the overlooked, and speeding selections—no reply.

sentences.zh: 已，復請重武科、復比試、清納級、汰家丁、恤班操、急邊餉，時亦不能用。

translations.literal: Later he again asked to restore the military examination, revive comparative testing, clarify purchased ranks, cut household retainers, relieve rotating guard duty, and hurry frontier pay—at the time these too could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again urged restoring the military exam, reviving comparative testing, clarifying purchased ranks, cutting household troops, relieving guard duty, and hurrying frontier pay—all ignored.

sentences.zh: 遼東巡撫楊鎬請用舊將李如梅，以僖言，改用張承蔭。

translations.literal: Liaodong Grand Coordinator Yang Hao asked to use the old general Li Rumei; on Xi's word, Zhang Chengyin was used instead.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong Grand Coordinator Yang Hao wanted the old general Li Rumei; on Xi's advice, Zhang Chengyin was used instead.

sentences.zh: 承蔭未至而鎮遠堡、曹莊相繼失事，鎬皆不以實聞。

translations.literal: Chengyin had not yet arrived when Zhenyuan Fort and Caozhuang fell in succession; Hao reported none of it truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chengyin arrived, Zhenyuan Fort and Caozhuang fell in succession; Hao reported none of it truthfully.

sentences.zh: 僖兩疏劾之，鎬旋引去。

translations.literal: Xi impeached him in two memorials, and Hao soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xi impeached him twice, and Hao soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已，與同官孫振基等劾熊廷弼殺人媚人。

translations.literal: Later, with his colleague Sun Zhenji and others, he impeached Xiong Tingbi for killing men to please others.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Sun Zhenji impeached Xiong Tingbi for killing men to please others.

sentences.zh: 又言湯賓尹取韓敬，關節顯然，語具《振基傳》。

translations.literal: He also said Tang Binyin took Han Jing through obvious string-pulling; the details are in the biography of Zhenji.
translations.idiomatic: He also exposed Tang Binyin's obvious string-pulling for Han Jing; details are in Zhenji's biography.

sentences.zh: 尋乞假歸。

translations.literal: Soon he asked leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 四十五年京察，賓尹黨用事，以僖倚附東林，謫山西按察知事。

translations.literal: At the capital evaluation in the forty-fifth year the Binyin faction was in power; because Xi leaned on the Donglin faction, he was demoted to Surveillance Commissioner in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the year-45 capital evaluation the Binyin faction ruled; Xi was demoted to Shanxi surveillance commissioner for leaning on Donglin.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，起兵部主事，歷尚寶丞、少卿，改太常。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was raised as a principal clerk in the Ministry of War, served in succession as Vice Director and Vice Minister of the Imperial Seals Office, and was transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he rose in the Ministry of War, served in the Imperial Seals Office, and transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，魏忠賢黨御史陳世飐劾之，遂落職。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year the Wei Zhongxian faction censor Chen Shichou impeached him, and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year five Wei Zhongxian's censor Chen Shichou impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官，致仕家居。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored; he retired and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen his office was restored; he retired home.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，李自成陷慶陽，僖死之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year Li Zicheng took Qingyang, and Xi died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year sixteen Li Zicheng took Qingyang, and Xi died.

sentences.zh: 王道純，字懷鞠，蒲城人。

translations.literal: Wang Daochun, courtesy name Huaiju, was a native of Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daochun, styled Huaiju, came from Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: He became jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Tianqi 5.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年擢御史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was promoted censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 3 he was promoted censor.

sentences.zh: 疏陳破資格之說，言銓除、舉劾、考選，甲乙科太低昂，宜變通，則賢才日廣。

translations.literal: He memorialized on breaking rigid qualification rules, saying that in appointments, impeachments, and examinations the grades of jia and yi were set too high or low and should be made flexible, then worthy talent would daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on breaking rigid qualifications, saying appointment, impeachment, and examination grades were too rigid and should be flexible so worthy talent would grow.

sentences.zh: 帝命所司即行，而甲科勢重，卒不能返。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to carry it out at once, but the jia grade faction was powerful and in the end it could not be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered it carried out, but the jia-grade faction was too powerful and nothing changed.

sentences.zh: 流賊躪關中，道純請急振饑民，毋使從賊，報可。

translations.literal: Roving bandits trampled Guanzhong; Daochun asked urgently to relieve the starving people and keep them from joining bandits; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: As roving bandits ravaged Guanzhong, Daochun urged urgent relief so the starving would not join them; approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 已，劾罷光祿卿蘇晉、參政張爾基。

translations.literal: Later he impeached and removed Minister of Imperial Entertainments Su Jin and Pacification Commissioner Zhang Erji.
translations.idiomatic: Later he impeached and removed Su Jin and Zhang Erji.

sentences.zh: 四年，劾吏部尚書王永光當去者三，不可留者四，不納。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he impeached Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang with three reasons he ought to leave and four why he could not remain; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he gave three reasons Wang Yongguang should leave and four why he could not stay; the emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 巡按山東。

translations.literal: He toured and inspected Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He toured Shandong as censor.

sentences.zh: 其時李九成、孔有德叛於吳橋，南下。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jiucheng and Kong Youde rebelled at Wuqiao and marched south.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Jiucheng and Kong Youde rebelled at Wuqiao and marched south.

sentences.zh: 道純移書巡撫余大成，令討捕，大成不信。

translations.literal: Daochun sent a letter to Grand Coordinator Yu Dacheng ordering pursuit and capture; Dacheng did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Daochun wrote Grand Coordinator Yu Dacheng ordering pursuit; Dacheng did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 再促之，遂托疾請告，與登萊巡撫孫元化遣使招撫。

translations.literal: When urged again, Dacheng pleaded illness and asked leave, and with Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Sun Yuanhua sent envoys to offer pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Urged again, Dacheng pleaded illness and, with Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Sun Yuanhua, sent envoys to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 道純以為非，請敕二撫速剿。

translations.literal: Daochun thought this wrong and asked that both coordinators be urgently ordered to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Daochun thought this wrong and asked that both coordinators be ordered to suppress them at once.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷登州，元化被縶，大成猶主招撫。

translations.literal: When the bandits took Dengzhou, Yuanhua was seized, yet Dacheng still favored pacification.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels took Dengzhou and seized Yuanhua, Dacheng still favored pacification.

sentences.zh: 道純憤，抗疏力爭，帝即命道純監軍。

translations.literal: Daochun in anger submitted a defiant memorial arguing strenuously; the emperor at once ordered Daochun to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: Daochun angrily memorialized in protest; the emperor at once ordered him to supervise the army.

sentences.zh: 及徐從治代大成，謝璉代元化，並入萊州，為賊困。

translations.literal: When Xu Congzhi replaced Dacheng and Xie Lian replaced Yuanhua, both entered Laizhou and were trapped by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Congzhi replaced Dacheng and Xie Lian replaced Yuanhua, both entered Laizhou and were trapped.

sentences.zh: 在外調度，止道純一人。

translations.literal: Of those directing affairs outside, only Daochun remained.
translations.idiomatic: Of those directing affairs outside, only Daochun remained.

sentences.zh: 賊遣人偽乞撫，道純焚書斬使，馳疏言：「賊日以撫愚我，一撫而六城陷，再撫而登州亡，三撫而黃縣失，今四撫而萊州被圍。

translations.literal: The bandits sent men falsely suing for pacification; Daochun burned their letters and beheaded the envoys, and sent an urgent memorial saying: "The bandits daily use pacification to fool us—one pacification and six cities fell, a second and Dengzhou was lost, a third and Huangxian was taken; now a fourth and Laizhou is besieged.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent false peace envoys; Daochun burned their letters and beheaded them, memorializing urgently: "Pacification fools us—one round and six cities fell, a second and Dengzhou was lost, a third and Huangxian fell; now a fourth and Laizhou is besieged.

sentences.zh: 我軍屢挫，安能復戰？

translations.literal: Our army has been repeatedly defeated—how can we fight again?
translations.idiomatic: Our army has been repeatedly defeated—how can we fight again?

sentences.zh: 乞速發大軍，拯此危土。」

translations.literal: I beg that a great army be sent quickly to save this endangered land."
translations.idiomatic: Send a great army quickly to save this endangered land."

sentences.zh: 時周延儒、熊明遇主撫議，道純反被責讓。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Yanru and Xiong Mingyu favored pacification, and Daochun was instead rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yanru and Xiong Mingyu favored pacification, and Daochun was rebuked instead.

sentences.zh: 明遇遣職方主事張國臣贊畫軍事，國臣入賊中招諭。

translations.literal: Mingyu sent Bureau of War principal clerk Zhang Guochen to assist in military planning; Guochen entered the bandit camp to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyu sent Zhang Guochen of the Bureau of War to plan the campaign; Guochen entered the rebel camp to win them over.

sentences.zh: 賊佯許之，攻圍如故。

translations.literal: The bandits pretended to agree, but attacked and besieged as before.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pretended to agree but attacked and besieged as before.

sentences.zh: 及總督劉宇烈至，進兵沙河，道純與之俱。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Liu Yulie arrived and advanced to Shahe, Daochun went with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Liu Yulie arrived and advanced to Shahe, Daochun went with him.

sentences.zh: 宇烈中情怯，頓兵不進，日議撫，尋棄軍奔。

translations.literal: Yulie was cowardly at heart, halted the army and did not advance, daily discussed pacification, and soon abandoned the army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yulie was cowardly, halted the army, daily discussed pacification, and soon fled.

sentences.zh: 道純復請速討，不納。

translations.literal: Daochun again asked for swift suppression; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Daochun again urged swift suppression; he was ignored.

sentences.zh: 迨巡撫謝璉被執，帝震怒，逮宇烈，召道純還京，而明遇亦罷去。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Xie Lian was seized, the emperor was shaken with anger, arrested Yulie, summoned Daochun back to the capital, and Mingyu was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Lian was seized, the emperor was furious, arrested Yulie, recalled Daochun, and dismissed Mingyu.

sentences.zh: 宇烈下吏，引道純分過。

translations.literal: Yulie was sent to the magistrates and cited Daochun to share the blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yulie was prosecuted and cited Daochun to share the blame.

sentences.zh: 道純疏駁其所奏十余事，命所司並按。

translations.literal: Daochun memorialized rebutting more than ten items in his report and ordered the relevant offices to investigate all together.
translations.idiomatic: Daochun rebutted more than ten items in his report and ordered a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 又劾明遇、國臣交通誤國十罪，語侵延儒。

translations.literal: He also impeached Mingyu and Guochen with ten crimes of collusion that harmed the state, wording that touched Zhou Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Mingyu and Guochen on ten counts of collusion harming the state, implicating Zhou Yanru.

sentences.zh: 疏未下，延儒泄之國臣，國臣亦劾道純十罪，道純遂並劾延儒。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was issued, Yanru leaked it to Guochen; Guochen also impeached Daochun with ten crimes, and Daochun then impeached Yanru as well.
translations.idiomatic: Before it was issued, Yanru leaked it to Guochen; Guochen impeached Daochun on ten counts, and Daochun impeached Yanru in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不問。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired into none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inquired into none of it.

sentences.zh: 已而賊平，道純竟坐監軍溺職，斥為民。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Daochun was still punished for neglect of duty as army supervisor and dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, Daochun was still punished for neglect as army supervisor and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十五年以廷臣薦，將起用，未果。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, on court recommendation, he was about to be recalled but it did not come about.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen the court recommended recalling him, but it did not happen.

sentences.zh: 及李自成陷蒲城，道純抗節死。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took Pucheng, Daochun died resisting to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng took Pucheng, Daochun died defiantly.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈恤如制。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted condolence according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted condolence as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 田時震，富平人。

translations.literal: Tian Shizhen was a native of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shizhen came from Fuping.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He became jinshi in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Tianqi 2.

sentences.zh: 歷知光山、靈寶。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Guangshan and Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Guangshan and Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年入為御史，疏劾南京戶部尚書範濟世、順天巡撫單明詡、御史卓邁黨逆罪，而請免故御史夏之令誣坐贓，並從之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he entered as a censor, memorializing to impeach Nanjing Minister of Revenue Fan Jishi, Shuntian Grand Coordinator Shan Mingxu, and Censor Zhuo Mai for factional treason, and asking exemption for the former censor Xia Zhiling, falsely convicted of embezzlement—all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 he became a censor, impeached Fan Jishi, Shan Mingxu, and Zhuo Mai for factional treason, and secured exemption for Xia Zhiling's false embezzlement conviction—all granted.

sentences.zh: 劾劉鴻訓納田仰金，囑吏部尚書王永光用為四川巡撫，仰迄罷去。

translations.literal: He impeached Liu Hongxun for taking Tian Yang's gold and instructing Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang to appoint Yang Sichuan grand coordinator; Yang was dismissed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Liu Hongxun for taking Tian Yang's gold and having Wang Yongguang appoint Yang grand coordinator of Sichuan; Yang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時震以發鴻訓私，進秩一等。

translations.literal: Shizhen was promoted one rank for exposing Hongxun's private conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen was promoted one rank for exposing Hongxun.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又劾永光及溫體仁，忤旨切責。

translations.literal: Before long he again impeached Yongguang and Wen Tiren; going against the imperial will, he was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he impeached Yongguang and Wen Tiren and was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 御史袁弘勛者，永光心腹也，被劾罷職，永光力援之。

translations.literal: The censor Yuan Hongxun was Yongguang's intimate; impeached and dismissed, Yongguang strongly supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yuan Hongxun, Yongguang's intimate, was impeached and dismissed; Yongguang strongly supported him.

sentences.zh: 時震言：「弘勛因閣臣劉鴻訓賄敗，輒肆瀆辯。

translations.literal: Shizhen said: "Hongxun, because Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun was ruined by bribery, then indulged in insolent argument.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen said, "Hongxun, because Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun fell to bribery, indulges in insolent argument.

sentences.zh: 不知鴻訓之差快人意者，正以能別白徐大化、霍維華諸人之奸而斥去之，安得借此為翻案之端耶？

translations.literal: He does not know that what made Hongxun's fall satisfying was precisely that he could distinguish the treachery of Xu Dahua, Huo Weihua, and others and drive them out—how can this be made a pretext to overturn the cases?
translations.idiomatic: He does not see that Hongxun's fall was satisfying because he exposed Xu Dahua, Huo Weihua, and others—how can this reopen those cases?

sentences.zh: 弘勛計行，大化、維華輩將乘間抵隙，害不可勝言。」

translations.literal: If Hongxun's plan succeeds, Dahua, Weihua, and their kind will seize every opening; the harm cannot be told."
translations.idiomatic: If Hongxun succeeds, Dahua, Weihua, and their kind will seize every opening; the harm is incalculable."

sentences.zh: 因薦故光祿少卿史記事，蕭然四壁，講學著書，亟宜召用，帝不納。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended the former Vice Minister of Imperial Entertainments Shi Jishi, whose four walls were bare, who lectured and wrote books, and ought urgently to be summoned— the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended the former Vice Minister Shi Jishi, who lived in bare rooms lecturing and writing, and ought urgently to be recalled—the emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 時震既屢忤永光，遂以年例出為江西右參議，調山西，就遷左參政，罷歸。

translations.literal: Shizhen, having repeatedly offended Yongguang, was transferred by seniority rule to Right Pacification Commissioner in Jiangxi, moved to Shanxi, was then made Left Pacification Commissioner, and dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Having repeatedly offended Yongguang, he was transferred by seniority to Jiangxi Right Pacification Commissioner, then Shanxi Left Pacification Commissioner, and dismissed home.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，流賊陷富平，授以偽職，不屈死。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year roving bandits took Fuping; he was offered a false office and died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year sixteen rebels took Fuping; offered a puppet post, he died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 同邑朱崇德，字淳庵，侍郎國棟父也。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Zhu Chongde, courtesy name Chun'an, was the father of Vice Minister Guodong.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Zhu Chongde, styled Chun'an, was Vice Minister Guodong's father.

sentences.zh: 國棟中天啟二年進士，歷戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Guodong became jinshi in the second year of Tianqi and served as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong took the jinshi in Tianqi 2 and served as Revenue Bureau supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎張捷薦逆案呂純如，國棟上疏力詆。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Zhang Jie recommended Lü Chunru of the treason cases; Guodong memorialized strenuously denouncing it.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhang Jie recommended treason-case figure Lü Chunru; Guodong memorialized in fierce protest.

sentences.zh: 已，又劾兩廣總督熊文燦，招撫海盜劉香，奏詞掩飾欺罔五罪，帝切責文燦。

translations.literal: Later he again impeached the Liang-Guang supreme coordinator Xiong Wencan for pacifying the pirate Liu Xiang, with five crimes of concealment and deception in his memorial; the emperor sharply rebuked Wencan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he impeached Liang-Guang supreme coordinator Xiong Wencan for pacifying the pirate Liu Xiang on five counts of concealment; the emperor sharply rebuked Wencan.

sentences.zh: 而國棟累遷巡撫山東右僉都御史，督治昌平。

translations.literal: Guodong was promoted in succession to Grand Coordinator of Shandong as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and supervised affairs at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong rose to Shandong Grand Coordinator as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and supervised Changping.

sentences.zh: 十五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year fifteen.

sentences.zh: 國棟卒之明年，富平陷於賊。

translations.literal: The year after Guodong died, Fuping fell to bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The year after Guodong died, Fuping fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊驅崇德往長安，中道稱病。

translations.literal: The bandits drove Chongde toward Chang'an; midway he claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drove Chongde toward Chang'an; midway he claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 賊見其老，以為果病也，聽之歸。

translations.literal: Seeing him old, the bandits thought he was truly ill and let him return.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing him old, the rebels thought him truly ill and let him return.

sentences.zh: 崇德曰：「始吾所以隱忍者，為九族計也，今得死所矣。」

translations.literal: Chongde said: "At first I endured in hiding for the sake of my nine clans; now I have found the place to die."
translations.idiomatic: Chongde said, "At first I endured in hiding for my clan's sake; now I have found the place to die."

sentences.zh: 乃北面再拜，自縊死。

translations.literal: He then faced north, bowed twice, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He faced north, bowed twice, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 是時關中諸死節者甫議恤，而國變至。

translations.literal: At that time condolence for the martyrs of Guanzhong was just being discussed when the dynastic catastrophe arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence for Guanzhong's martyrs was just being discussed when the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 福王立，始贈崇德右副都御史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu established his court, Chongde was first posthumously made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu ruled, Chongde was first posthumously made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：流賊荼毒中原，所至糜爛。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Roving bandits poisoned the Central Plain; wherever they went all was trampled to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Roving bandits poisoned the Central Plain; wherever they went all was ruined.

sentences.zh: 士大夫遘難者，不死則辱。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials who met calamity either died or were disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials who met calamity either died or were disgraced.

sentences.zh: 然當其時，徘徊隱忍、蒙垢而終以自戕者，亦不少矣。

translations.literal: Yet at that time those who hesitated, endured in hiding, bore shame, and in the end destroyed themselves were also not few.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many hesitated, endured in hiding, bore shame, and destroyed themselves in the end.

sentences.zh: 賀逢聖諸人從容就義，臨患難而不易其節，一死顧不重哉！

translations.literal: He Fengsheng and the others calmly accepted death, facing hardship without changing their integrity—is not one death weighty indeed!
translations.idiomatic: He Fengsheng and the others calmly accepted death and did not change their integrity in hardship—was their death not weighty indeed!

sentences.zh: 逢聖與南居益、周士樸公方清正，呂維祺邃學純修，固中朝賢士大夫。

translations.literal: Fengsheng with Nan Juyi and Zhou Shipu were upright and pure in public conduct; Lu Weiqi was deep in learning and pure in cultivation—they were truly worthy scholar-officials of the central court.
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng, Nan Juyi, and Zhou Shipu were upright and pure; Lu Weiqi was deep in learning and pure in conduct—truly worthy central-court scholars.

sentences.zh: 宋師襄所謂「上謾下欺，釀成大患」，末季之習，痛哉其言之也。

translations.literal: What Song Shixiang called "superiors deceive and subordinates cheat, brewing great calamity" was the habit of the dynasty's last days—how painful his words!
translations.idiomatic: Song Shixiang's words—"superiors deceive and subordinates cheat, brewing great calamity"—capture the habit of the dynasty's last days; how painful his warning!
